explanation: A gift consisting of grain or flour that was offered to God to show gratitude and submission.
Food, especially bread, that has not undergone the fermentation process, thus symbolizing purity and holiness.
An ingredient in the grain offering representing God's Spirit and blessing.
Fragrant substances burned to release a pleasing aroma, symbolizing prayers and devotion to God.
A part of the gift that is burned on the altar as a symbolic act to give something back to God and seek his favor.
The highest religious leader among the Israelites, responsible for performing ritual duties and sacrifices in the temple.
A symbol of an enduring covenant and loyalty between God and his people, used in the grain offering.
